piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diptych in two halves. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a film clapperboard and a coin with a dollar sign, under the label “Licence”. On the right, “Today”: the same clapperboard and the same coin crossed out with blue lines, under the label “Closed”.
piezas.titular: Disney was going to open its characters to AI; Sora shut down before the money arrived
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025 it was being said that Disney would allow content to be created with its characters, and the end of generative AI’s “free-for-all” was being predicted. The deal came in December, with Sora; in March, OpenAI shut Sora down and the deal fell apart.
cuerpo: On 14 November 2025, in EduMedia-IAG, a conversation about an AI-animated video clip turned to copyright. People said that Disney was going to allow content to be created with its characters, presumably for a fee, and ventured that once licences had to be paid for, free access to the models would come to an end.

On 11 December, Disney and OpenAI announced [a three-year licensing agreement](https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/press-releases/the-walt-disney-company-and-openai-reach-landmark-agreement-to-bring-beloved-characters-from-across-disneys-brands-to-sora/): more than 200 characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Star Wars for Sora videos, a selection of them on Disney+, and a $1bn investment by Disney in OpenAI. The first videos were expected in early 2026.

Neither the deal nor the tool lasted the year. On 24 March 2026, OpenAI announced that Sora would be shut down: the app and the website stopped working on 26 April, according to [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-sets-two-stage-sora-shutdown-with-app-closing-april-2026-and-api-following-in-september/), and the API on 24 September, according to [OpenAI’s deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Disney walked away from the deal and, according to Reuters, as reported by [Campus Technology](https://campustechnology.com/articles/2026/03/31/openai-drops-sora-short-form-ai-video-platform.aspx), no money had changed hands. Access was not closed because of licences: the tool was closed.

fuentes.titulo: The Walt Disney Company and OpenAI Reach Landmark Agreement to Bring Beloved Characters from Across Disney's Brands to Sora (11-12-2025)
OpenAI sets two-stage Sora shutdown, with app closing April 2026 and API following in September (The Decoder, 28-3-2026)
OpenAI Drops Sora Short-Form AI Video Platform (Campus Technology, 31-3-2026)

piezas.comprobado: Mensaje 6211 de EduMedia-IAG (t.me/EduMediaIAG/6211, 14-11-2025): Disney “ha abierto la veda”, “dentro de su plataforma y pagando”; la idea de que la “barra libre” desaparecerá con las licencias es del mensaje 6213 del mismo día. Comunicado de Disney (abierto): anuncio del 11-12-2025, licencia de tres años, más de 200 personajes de Disney, Marvel, Pixar y Star Wars, selección en Disney+, inversión de 1.000 millones de dólares, primeros vídeos a principios de 2026. Página de retiradas de OpenAI (abierta): Videos API y sora-2 avisados el 24-3-2026, cierre el 24-9-2026. The Decoder (abierta): app y web cerradas el 26-4-2026, API el 24-9-2026; el centro de ayuda de OpenAI, vía búsqueda, lo confirma. Campus Technology (abierta): Reuters, “no money has yet changed hands”, Disney respeta la decisión de OpenAI de salir del vídeo; la salida de Disney del acuerdo, confirmada además en varios medios por búsqueda. Fecha del anuncio, 24-3-2026, según la mayoría de fuentes (The Decoder fecha su artículo el 28). Nada repetido: publicado.txt no tiene piezas sobre Sora ni Disney y “Ya contado” no los toca (NotebookLM, el 6-11, queda descartado). Medida: 237 palabras con la entradilla.
